input.quote: 2.2 Internal Use License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Commerce One grants to Corio a nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license in the Territory to reproduce, install and use additional copies of the Software and Software tools and utilities, subject to any restrictions placed on the Commerce One by third party software providers, in machine executable object code for (i) Corio's internal business operations and (ii) production, testing, development, upgrade, reporting and training.
input.rationale:
The grants in Section 2 run to Corio alone. Section 2.1 is expressly "perpetual and irrevocable" and Section 2.2 is "fully paid up, perpetual", so revocability is not an issue, and transferability meets the fallback because Section 14.1 permits assignment without consent in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets (subject only to a direct-competitor consent carve-out). However, neither Section 2.2 nor any other provision extends the licence to our affiliates, and there is no defined "Affiliate" or any notice mechanism to add them; Section 2.2 is limited to "Corio's internal business operations". Contractor use is only indirectly addressed (Corio Servers may be "owned or operated by or for Corio"). Affiliate coverage is a material term of both the preferred and fallback positions, so the clause fails the fallback on that element. Our minimal edit adds affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf to the internal use licence, leaving the remaining grant architecture (including the unlimited Customer sublicence) untouched.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.72

ops.oldText: for (i) Corio's internal business operations and (ii) production, testing, development, upgrade, reporting and training.
ops.newText: for (i) the internal business operations of Corio and its affiliates and (ii) production, testing, development, upgrade, reporting and training, in each case including use by contractors acting on Corio's behalf.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the internal use licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, consistent with our playbook position that the grant cover affiliates and contractors; the licence otherwise remains perpetual, paid-up and assignable in an M&A transaction under Section 14.1.
proposal.summary: Add affiliates and contractors to the Section 2.2 internal use licence.
